newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt softens, crown firms on weaker mark.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt softens, crown firms on weaker mark.

text.p: 1545 GMT - Swedish debt yields rose on Tuesday pushed up by the higher German yields and the crown firmed on the back of the weaker mark with central bank intervention reported.
The Riksbank left the repo rate unchanged at 4.10 percent at its weekly operation, as expected.
* Six month T-bill rate up one basis point to 4.29 pct
* 10-year bond yield up five basis points to 6.57 pct
* Mark stable at 4.2950 against the crown compared to 4.2970 late on Monday and off the day's lows of 4.3240.
* Riksbank bought crowns at 4.3150-4.32 to the mark, a dealer said.
Swedish debt yields rose on Tuesday pushed up by higher German yields and the crown firmed on the back of the weaker mark with central bank intervention reported.
The 10-year bond yield rose five basis points to 6.57 percent and the six-month T-bill rate advanced one basis point to 4.29 percent.

The crown reversed early losses against the mark, boosted by a stronger dollar and the German Bundesbank's rate decision and was trading at 4.2950 to the mark late on Tuesday compared to 4.2970 late on Monday.
At about 1100 GMT the Riksbank intervened, buying crowns at around 4.3150-4.32 to mark, a dealer said.
"That sparked some commercial interest to buy crowns against dollars. It's possible that the Riksbank has an intra-day target for the TCW index," a dealer said.
The Riksbank has no official target for the crown but has said an appropriate range is 109-118 in real terms on the TCW index. The crown currently stands at 120.45.
The Riksbank left the repo rate unchanged at 4.10 percent at its weekly operation, as expected.
